_doc: Telegram trade alerts (owner message 2026-10-21). Every number the alert rules use lives in this file. Output-only: no paper or trading decision reads this file, the alert code or the alert state.
killed_opened_exception_label: ⚠️ KILLED STRATEGY (research) · PARITY TEST · observation only
_killed_opened_exception_doc: Owner rulings D150, D193(a), D194 (DECISIONS D221), v4: a source listed here whose status is KILLED alerts the signals its paper book OPENED (paper outcome 'opened') instead of SUPPRESSED_KILLED. Every other rule still applies (cost filter, entry-to-stop cost filter, LATE, dedup, rate limit, symbol exclusions, the D117 line). The alert, its follow-ups and its daily-summary line carry the label above right after the D117 line, and its result reply comes from the paper ledger (D149). Its not-opened signals stay SUPPRESSED_KILLED. allow_killed is unchanged and still applies to every other source. The shipped config leaves the list empty, and a config without the key behaves as v3; the v4 enabled copy (trade_alerts_config.enabled.v4.json) lists PASSED_BOOK.
_ledger_followup_doc: v4 (D149/D150): a sent alert whose trade result lives in a ledger (FWD-1 and FWD-3 trades: their own ledgers, read only; a killed_opened_exception trade: the paper ledger) gets that ledger's result as its reply, or 'result pending in FWD ledger' / 'result pending in paper ledger' once the alert-level tracker has ended without one. The tracker's own replies for those alerts are logged as LEVELS_ONLY, not posted. The alert stops waiting for its ledger after this many days.

cost._doc: Round trip = fees on both sides + entry slippage + exit slippage, read from the app's ResearchConfig defaults (taker_fee_rate, entry_slippage_rate, exit_slippage_rate). Skip as SKIPPED_COST when stop distance < multiple x round trip. A SCREENER signal is also skipped when |TP1 - stop| / signal close is under that same multiple (owner D63). The screener engine itself is not changed.

cost_stop._doc: Owner ruling D145 item 3: entry-to-stop cost filter, in addition to the cost check above and the screener TP1-to-stop band (both kept). Skip as SKIPPED_COST_STOP when |entry_ref - stop| / entry_ref < multiple x round trip, round trip = fee_sides x (taker_fee_rate + slippage_rate) = 2 x (0.0005 + 0.0002) = 0.0014 (the D144 real costs), cutoff 0.42%. These numbers are the alert's own, not the ResearchConfig defaults the 'cost' section reads.

_cost_stop_entry_ref_doc: Entry price the D145 entry-to-stop filter measures from: 'near_edge' = the entry-zone edge nearest the stop (the smallest distance, the worst fill inside the zone), or 'mid' = the entry-zone mid. Default near_edge. Conflict in the owner's text (D145): it says 'entry mid', but also says the second SOL alert of 2026-10-21 (bar 17:00 UTC, zone 108.54-108.12, SL 107.70, stop about 0.4%) must be skipped. At the mid (108.33) that stop is 0.58% away, above the 0.42% cutoff, so 'mid' would NOT skip it; at the near edge (108.12) it is 0.39%, below the cutoff, so 'near_edge' does. near_edge is the more conservative reading and matches the owner's stated expectation; set 'mid' to follow the literal text.
_screener_cost_ok_only_doc: Owner ruling D188 part 3: true sends a SCREENER alert only when its cost as R is OK, the same rule as the screener's Trade chances column: cost as R = 2 x (taker 0.05% + slippage 0.02%, 0.05% on AAVE/APT/ARB/DOT/ETC/OP/FIL) x entry / |entry - stop| <= 0.25, entry = the screener's entry price (the signal close when the row has none). Otherwise the signal is a SKIPPED_COST_R skip, never sent. Default false (no change). Other sources are not affected; every alert keeps the UNPROVEN line.

forward_runner._doc: Owner ruling D51b: scheduled forward runners (FWD-1, FWD-3) keep their frozen schedules; their records land after the bar close, so they get their own LATE limit and their alerts show the minutes since the signal bar close.

_journal_alert_outcomes_doc: P14 (owner ruling D51c): not-opened journal signals that carry the engine stop and TP1 (DECISION_JOURNAL_SIGNAL_DETAIL on) are read as signals; without them they stay NOT_OPENED skips. Since D145 a read not-opened signal is still not sent unless send_not_opened is true.
_send_not_opened_doc: Owner ruling D145 item 2: a paper-book signal (paper_book_sources, or any non-screener signal that carries a paper outcome) alerts only if the book OPENED it. Any other paper outcome is a NOT_OPENED skip carrying the paper reason, never sent and not tracked (the dry-run preview tracking of not-sent signals aside). true sends them anyway, with the line '❌ NOT OPENED: <reason>' right after the UNPROVEN line. Screener signals have no paper outcome and are not affected.

symbol_exclusions._doc: Owner rulings D108/D120: BTC is for non-directional strategies only, so there is no directional BTC alert. A signal from a listed source on a listed symbol is logged as an EXCLUDED_SYMBOL skip with this reason and is never sent, rendered or tracked. Alerting only: the forward tests and live paper are not touched. CANDLE12_V2 (BTC-only) is dropped from the sources entirely (D120).

sources._lcsc_fwd3_target_r_doc: LCSC FWD-3 contract: target 2R off the signal close (stop = invalidation); used because the run record lists the target only once the trade is filled.
